_note: what each platform publishes about its own username form, carried as data so the reader can see the rule it applied. verified is false on every entry: these were read from platform announcements and their own posts, not from a reference page fetched today, and no probe here can check a username without messaging a stranger.
_limit: only the rules marked fatal decide validity. a length or a character set is reported as outside_shape instead, because a wrong bound must not make the tool call a real person's handle invalid.

signal.shape: a nickname, a dot, then a numeric discriminator, e.g. alice.42
sources: signal's own announcement, 2024-02: usernames exist so a chat does not need a phone number
signal's own post: usernames are designed to be easily changeable, and signal keeps a hash of the username rather than the username
notes: a username is enough to start a chat, which is the point: no number required on either side
because signal stores a hash and people change their username, a username is a handle and not an identity
signal adds the discriminator itself when you share, so a bare nickname is not a username anybody can be reached on

whatsapp.shape: a handle, optionally written with a leading @, e.g. @alice
whatsapp.key: a four digit username key can be required before a chat starts, so knowing the exact username is not always enough
sources: whatsapp's username rollout reported 2026-06, with username reservation ahead of a wider launch
reporting on the rollout: no public directory, no suggestions, and an optional four digit username key
notes: no directory and no search: somebody has to give you the exact username, which is why it works as a contact handle
the four digit key is a barrier a lookup cannot see, and asking for it is a conversation rather than a check
a business keeps its phone number visible, so a business handle is not a private contact
